context:
w0 must NOT reuse the commit-split figure quoted anywhere in this project's review history without re-deriving it. A 2026-08-23 review pass produced '714 of 991 commits (72%) touched only process files' and that figure is WRONG: the classifier used 'grep -qv', and this machine's grep is ugrep, where -q reports whether any line MATCHED and ignores the -v inversion, so any commit containing a process path scored process-only. Two independent adversarial reviewers caught it.

Corrected, reproducible measurements over 991 commits since 2026-06-01:
 - Process-only commits: 208 of 991 (21%). An independent reviewer got ~200 by the same definition.
 - Commits touching benchbox/: 373 of 991 (37.6%).
 - Line churn excluding the bulk results-data/ JSON: agent and tracker process files 389,833 (60.7%); shipped Python package 65,051 (10.1%); process-scaffolding tests 57,286 (8.9%); results explorer 6,038 (0.9%); user docs 4,226 (0.7%).
 - Standing surface: 31 CI workflows; 151 Makefile targets (191 in make/inventory.json); 1,796-line Makefile plus 584 lines across make/*.mk; 133 of 1,343 test_*.py files (9.9%) test process scaffolding.

So the commit-count story is unremarkable and the CHURN story is the real one: roughly six lines of hand-written change go into tracker and agent-process files for every one that goes into the thing customers install. Frame w3's re-measure on churn, not commit counts.

DECISION GATE at w2: choose ratio cap, freeze list, or no cap, and record the reason. No cap is a legitimate outcome; leaving it unexamined is not.

Keep every safety gate. The target is discretionary process ENGINEERING, not the checks that protect releases and privacy: the UAT release-gate evidence, corpus privacy scrubbing, submission validation and release rollback targets all stay. Adversarial review on 2026-08-23 specifically rejected removing them, because v0.3.0 shipped a broken install.

anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD use 21% of commits and the 60.7%/10.1% churn split
anti_patterns.why: it was an artifact of ugrep's -qv semantics and is wrong

anti_patterns.dont: Delete or disable the UAT, privacy, submission or release-evidence gates under this item
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD target only discretionary process engineering
anti_patterns.why: they exist because v0.3.0 shipped a broken install and adversarial review rejected removing them

anti_patterns.dont: Implement a blocking CI gate that fails builds on a churn ratio
anti_patterns.instead: INSTEAD make it an observable report
anti_patterns.why: that adds process to solve a process problem

preserves.behavior: Every existing safety gate stays: UAT release-gate evidence, corpus privacy scrubbing, submission validation, release rollback targets
Worktree write policy, commit identity policy and the no-agent-attribution rule are unaffected

verifications.command: run the w0 script over git history since 2026-06-01
verifications.expected: process-to-product churn ratio reported and matching the recorded figure within rounding
